newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras signs economic goal plan with IMF.
newsitem.headline: Honduras signs economic goal plan with IMF.

text.p: Honduras has signed a "monitored" agreement with the International Monetary Fund that will give the country access to some $190 million in past-due credits, a government official said on Wednesday.
"We can say that on April 8 a deal was agreed between Honduras and the IMF. It is an accord known as a 'monitored' plan," said Guillermo Bueso, the director of the economic cabinet.
Bueso spoke to HRN Radio from Washington, where he said both sides had signed the agreement, which outlines the country's economic goals for 1997.
Bueso said the plan would allow Honduras to access $190 million in credits, of which $46.2 million would be disbursed on Friday by the World Bank.
"This agreement permits us to access new credits and also credits that have been overdue since last year because we were unable to meet our economic targets," he said.

Under the plan, Honduras agreed to a goal of 4.5 percent economic growth, a fiscal deficit of 2.5 percent of gross domestic product, inflation of between 15 and 16 percent and an international reserves goal of at least three months' worth of imports.
Last year, Honduras' economy grew 3.4 percent, the fiscal deficit was 3.5 percent and inflation was 24.9 percent.
The agreement was a stopgap measure after Honduras' failure to agree with the IMF earlier this year on a "letter of intent."
"This agreement is a success for Honduras because it maintains our internal and external credibility with both investors and international financial institutions," Bueso said.
Bueso said the economy would grow more this year due to strong growth in private investment. He said the government would maintain strict controls over public spending to control the fiscal deficit.
He said Honduras would lower its tax on imported raw materials in May from five to three percent and again in December to one percent.
Bueso added that a tax on banana exports, the country's second leading export, would be cut from 50 centavos per 18-kilo box to 20 centavos in July.
